faqs.question: What is SFURTI?
faqs.answer: To make the traditional industries more productive and competitive and facilitating their sustainable development, the Govt. of India announced in 2005-06, setting up of a fund for regeneration of traditional industries. Pursuant to this announcement, a Central Sector Scheme titled the "Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)" was launched.

faqs.question: Which ministry is implementing this scheme?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises is implementing the scheme with a view to organizing traditional industries and artisans into clusters to make them competitive and increase their income.

faqs.question: What are the objectives of SFURTI?
faqs.answer:
To develop clusters of traditional industries in the country over a period of five years.
To make traditional industries more competitive, market-driven, productive, and profitable.
To strengthen the cluster governance systems with the active participation of the stakeholders.
To build up innovative and traditional skills, improved technologies, advanced processes, market intelligence, and new models of public-private partnerships, so as to gradually replicate similar models of cluster-based regenerated traditional industries.

faqs.question: Who can apply for SFURTI?
faqs.answer:
Following is the list of organisations/institutions that can apply for SFRUTI:
Non-Government Organizations (NGOs)
Institutions of the Central and State Governments
Semi-Government institutions
Field functionaries of State and Central Government
Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)

faqs.question: What is the duration of Project?
faqs.answer: The time frame for implementation of Project will be 3 years.

faqs.question: How many types of Interventions are covered under Scheme?
faqs.answer: The Scheme covers three types of interventions: Soft Interventions, Hard Intervention & Thematic Interventions

faqs.question: What the activities covered under Soft Intervention?
faqs.answer:
Soft Interventions under the project would consist of activities such as
i. General Awareness, counseling, motivation and Trust building
ii. Skill development and Capacity Building
iii. Institutional development
iv. Exposure visits
v. Market Promotion initiatives
vi. Design and Product Development
vii. Participation in seminars, workshops and training programmes on
technology up-gradations, etc.

faqs.question: What the facilities covered under Hard Intervention?
faqs.answer:
Hard interventions will include creation of following facilities:
i. Creation of Common Facility Centres (CFCs)
ii. Raw Material Banks (RMBs)
iii. Up-gradation of Production Infrastructure
iv. Tools and Technological up-gradation such as Charkha upgradation, tool-kits distribution, etc
v. Warehousing Facility
vi. Training Centre
vii. Value addition and processing centre
Note: The assistance for raw material bank (RMB) shall be leveraged with financial institution for enhanced credit.

faqs.question: Whether the cost of land is included in the project cost?
faqs.answer: No. Land should be owned by Implementing Agency.

faqs.question: Who can play the role of Implementing Agencies (I.A.)?
faqs.answer:
Implementing Agencies (IAs) would be non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), Institutions of the Central and State Governments and Semi-Government Institutions, field functionaries of State & Central Government Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), etc suitable expertise to undertake cluster development. One IA may normally be assigned only one cluster (unless it is an agency with State-wide coverage). The selection of IAs, based on their regional reputation and experience of working at the grass-roots level, will be done by the Nodal Agencies (NAs), on the basis of transparent criteria. Private sector participation shall also be encouraged for the
implementation of the cluster projects. Corporate entities can also take up projects directly by forming cluster-specific SPVs. Corporates and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) foundations with expertise in cluster development will be encouraged to participate as IAs.

faqs.question: Can implementing agencies take up more than one traditional industry?
faqs.answer:
No. One Implementing Agency may normally be assigned only one cluster (unless it is an
agency with State-wide coverage).

faqs.question: Who can play the role of Technical Agencies (T.A.)?
faqs.answer: Established national/ regional level institutions, with proven expertise in artisanal and small enterprise cluster development shall be empanelled as Technical Agencies by Nodal Agency (N.A.) only can play the role of Technical Agency (T.A).

faqs.question: What is the definition of “Traditional Industry”?
faqs.answer: Broadly, ,,traditional industry" means an activity which produces marketable products, using locally available raw materials and skills and indigenous technology. Traditional Industry Cluster, in the Context of this document, refers to a geographical concentration of a sizable number of artisans or micro-enterprises, suppliers of raw materials, traders, service providers, etc. producing, processing, and servicing the same or similar types of products and facing common opportunities and threats

faqs.question: What is Coir?
faqs.answer: Coir is generally referred to as "Golden Fibre", which is a bye-product of coconut, extracted from the coconut husk.

faqs.question: What is the definition of “Traditional Industry”?
faqs.answer:
Broadly, "traditional industry" means an activity which produces marketable products, using
locally available raw material and skills and indigenous technology. Traditional Industry Cluster,
in the context of this document, refers to a geographical concentration of a sizable number of artisans or micro enterprises, suppliers of raw materials, traders, service providers, etc. producing, processing and servicing the same or similar types of products and facing common opportunities and threats.

faqs.question: What is a cluster?
faqs.answer: Clusters are defined as "geographical concentrations of inter-connected enterprises and associated institutions that face common challenges and opportunities". This definition highlights two essential features of clusters: they consist of a critical mass of enterprises located in geographical proximity to each other and enterprises within them share many common features.

faqs.question: What is the CFC?
faqs.answer:
Common Facility Centre (CFC) is one of the Components in Hard Intervention where which
artisans/end users can utilize the machineries installed thereon and manufacture coir based
value added products. CFC can also be used as a warehouse for storing and maintaining
finished products.

faqs.question: How to apply for SFRUTI?
faqs.answer: The above eligible agency/organization has to submit the proposal online through the SFURTI Portal (https://sfurti.msme.gov.in/SFURTI/SignUp.aspx) and the same is to be scrutinized at the State Level and Zonal Level before submitting it to the Scheme Steering Committee for approval.

name: Incentive Scheme for Establishment of New Super Specialty Hospital in Private Sector
brief_description: The scheme offers financial incentives (capital subsidy, interest subvention, and electricity duty reimbursement) to private/NGO entities establishing new super specialty hospitals (50+ beds) in Gujarat, targeting underserved areas.
details: Launched on 13th December 2016, the "Incentive Scheme for Establishment of New Super Specialty Hospital in Private Sector" by the Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to address the shortage of high-end medical facilities in remote areas by incentivizing private and non-governmental organizations to establish super specialty hospitals. The scheme provides 10% capital subsidy on medical equipment loans (up to ₹10 crore), 4% interest subvention (max ₹40 crore loan) for 7 years, and reimbursement of electricity duty for 5 years. Eligible entities include registered doctors, firms, trusts, and corporations.
benefits:
> **Capital Subsidy**

- 10% of bank loans for medical equipment (max ₹10 crore).
- Disbursed post-hospital operationalization.

> **Interest Subvention**

- 4% interest relief on loans up to ₹40 crore for 7 years.
- Paid in 6 annual installments after a 1-year grace period.

> **Electricity Duty Reimbursement**

100% reimbursement for 5 years (quarterly claims).
> **Employment Generation**

Mandates hiring qualified medical/paramedical staff.
> **Disbursement**

- **Capital Subsidy:** After Equipment Installation and Hospital Launch.- **Interest Subvention:** Annual Installments Post 1-Year Grace Period.- **Electricity Reimbursement:** Quarterly Claims.
exclusions: Excludes Government/Semi-Government Bodies.
eligibility:
> **The Following Entities Are Eligible**

- Registered Doctors (Gujarat Medical Council).
- Partnership Firms, Companies, Trusts, Societies, Cooperatives.

> **Hospital Requirements**

- 50+ Total Beds,including 10+ Super Specialty Beds.
- Covers Specialties Like Cardiology, Neurology, Oncology, etc. (List Expandable by Government).

> **Loan Conditions**

- Only Loans for Construction/Equipment (Excludes Land/Working Capital).

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take a printout of the [prescribed format](https://gujhealth.gujarat.gov.in/images/pdf/Application-forms-for-Establishment-of-New-Super-Specialty-Hospital-new.pdf) of the application form.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to - ***Commissioner, Health & Medical Education, Dr. Jivraj Mehta Bhavan, Gandhinagar***. Pay ₹20,000/- scrutiny fee via Demand Draft.
**Step 4:** Request a receipt or acknowledgement from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date of submission.

**Approval & Verification**

- State-Level Committee scrutinizes applications.
- Technical Group conducts physical inspections.

**Compliance**

- Submit quarterly utilization reports.
- Maintain services for 7 years (penalty: repayment if violated).

documents_required: Deed of Undertaking (₹100/- Stamp Paper) Committing to:
Compliance With Staffing and Service Norms.

faqs.question: Which specific medical specialties are covered under this super specialty hospital scheme's definition?

faqs.question: What types of financial assistance are available under this scheme for establishing new super specialty hospitals?
faqs.answer:

faqs.question: What are the key eligibility criteria for private healthcare providers to avail benefits under this scheme?

faqs.question: Which expenses are covered and excluded under the bank loan assistance component of this scheme?
faqs.answer:

faqs.question: What are the mandatory operational commitments that beneficiaries must adhere to under this scheme?
faqs.answer:
**Key requirements include:**

- Not relocating purchased medical equipment.

- Joining the MA/MA Vatsalya Scheme.
- Complying with all healthcare regulations.

faqs.question: How does the interest subvention component of this scheme work for eligible hospitals?
faqs.answer:
**The scheme provides:**

- 4% interest relief on approved bank loans.
- Maximum loan ceiling of ₹40 crore.
- Subvention paid annually for 7 years (first payment after 1 year of operation).
- Total of 7 installment payments.

faqs.question: What is the application process and timeline for availing benefits under this super specialty hospital scheme?
faqs.answer:

- Undergo technical committee verification.

faqs.question: What are the key conditions regarding electricity duty reimbursement under this scheme?

faqs.question: What legal obligations and undertakings must beneficiaries comply with under this scheme?
faqs.answer:

- Allow periodic inspections by authorities

faqs.question: How does the scheme prevent double-dipping or misuse of government incentives?
faqs.answer:

- Exclusion if similar benefits received.
- Bar on equipment subsidy duplication.
- Mandatory 7-year operational commitment.
- Recovery provisions for violations.

faqs.question: What is the composition and role of the State Level Committee that oversees this scheme?

**The committee comprises:**

- Hospital administrators.
- Technical subject experts.
- Roles include proposal scrutiny, assistance sanctioning, and monitoring compliance.

**Step 1:** Go to the Passport Seva Kendra where the appointment has been booked.
**Step 2:** Remember to carry the originals of the documents that you provided for your application. To be on the safe side, carry some self-attested copies as well.
**Step 3:** Carry a copy of the online payment receipt as well. An SMS receipt will do as well.
**Step 4:** Head to the pre-verification counter to collect your token.
**Step 5:** When it is your turn (as per the token), go to counter A to submit your documents.
**Step 6:** Following this, you will be called to Counter B. Here a verification officer will verify the documents and details you have submitted.
**Step 7:** Finally, a granting officer will review your application and decide whether or not to grant your application. Upon approving your application, the granting officer will send a request for police verification of your case.
Once your police verification report comes in and it is clear, the authorities issue your passport. It gets printed, laminated, and finally dispatched to your address. The whole process takes anywhere between 25 and 30 days under the normal mode.
**REIMBURSEMENT OF PASSPORT FEE**
The Government of Haryana will bear the cost of the passport fee. After issuance of the Passport, the Student needs to apply for the reimbursement of the fee. The college will reimburse the fee to the student who applied through this portal. 
**Step 1:** Visit the [Official Website](https://passport.highereduhry.ac.in/) of the Free Passport Scheme.
**Step 2:** Click on the " Apply for Passport Fees Reimbursement."
**Step 3:** You will land on the [Login Page. Login using your login credentials (Credentials are the same as "ERP Portal" for Login).](https://erp.highereduhry.ac.in/passportlogin.aspx)
[**Step 4:** Fill out the Fee Reimbursement Form upload a copy of the passport and click on submit.](https://erp.highereduhry.ac.in/passportlogin.aspx)
> **Verification by College**

> The college will verify the details of the student who applied for fee reimbursement.

> **Payment Challan Generation by Head Office**

> After verification, the college will generate the Challan/EPS on the eSalary website.

> **Fee Reimbursement from the Treasury**

> After clearance of the bill from the treasury, the amount will be credited to the student.

Secondary school-leaving certificate or a certificate issued from a recognised board.

faqs.question: What is the Free Passport Scheme, and who implements it?
faqs.answer: The Free Passport Scheme is an initiative by the Department of Higher Education, Government of Haryana, to reimburse passport fees for final-year UG and PG students in government colleges.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the Free Passport Scheme?
faqs.answer: Final-year UG and PG students studying in government colleges in Haryana are eligible. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Haryana or have completed Class 10 from the Haryana Board of School Education.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available for students of private colleges?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is only available for students enrolled in government colleges in Haryana.

faqs.question: What expenses does the Free Passport Scheme cover?
faqs.answer: The scheme reimburses the passport application fee of [?]1,500 for eligible students after the successful issuance of the passport.

faqs.question: Do students need to pay the passport fee first and then apply for reimbursement?
faqs.answer: Yes, students must pay the passport application fee during the application process and later apply for reimbursement through their respective colleges.

faqs.question: How can a student apply for passport fee reimbursement?
faqs.answer: Students must log in to the Department Portal, fill out the Fee Reimbursement Form, and upload a copy of their issued passport.

faqs.question: What happens after a student submits the reimbursement application?
faqs.answer: The college verifies the student's details. After verification, the college generates a Challan/EPS on the eSalary website for processing by the head office.

faqs.question: When will students receive the reimbursement amount?
faqs.answer: After the bill is cleared by the treasury, the reimbursed amount will be credited directly to the student's bank account.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for the passport?
faqs.answer: Students need an Aadhaar Card, proof of address, birth certificate or secondary school certificate, student ID card, bona fide certificate, and attested photocopies of certificates from the institution.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum attendance requirement to be eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, students must have a minimum of 80% attendance in the academic year to qualify.

faqs.question: How long does it take for the passport to be issued?
faqs.answer: The passport issuance process takes approximately 25 to 30 days under the normal application mode.

faqs.question: Where should students submit their passport application?
faqs.answer: Students must apply through the Passport Seva portal, fill in the required details, schedule an appointment, and visit the Passport Seva Kendra with the necessary documents.

faqs.question: What happens if a student's reimbursement application is rejected?
faqs.answer: If the application is rejected due to incorrect or missing details, students should contact their college authorities for clarification and reapply if necessary.

faqs.question: Can a student apply if they already hold a passport?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is only applicable to students applying for a passport for the first time.

name: Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit for the Construction Workers
brief_description: The "Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit for the Construction Workers" by the Sikkim BOCW Welfare Board, Labour Department, is a welfare scheme of the board that provides financial assistance is provided to the nominees/ dependents of a member, in case of his/her death or Permanent Disability.
details: The "Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit for the Construction Workers" by the Sikkim Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, is a welfare scheme for the registered workers of the board. Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to the nominees/ dependents of a member, in case of his/her death or Permanent Disability.
benefits: - ₹1,50,000/- is provided for Death Benefit.
eligibility:
> **For Registration as a Building/ Construction Worker:**

 - The applicant should be a resident of Sikkim.
 - The applicant should be a Building/ Construction Worker.
 - The applicant should be between 18 and 60 years.
 - The applicant should have served the Board for at least 90 days in a given year.

> **For the Application of the Welfare Scheme:**

 - Should be a nominee/ dependent of the registered worker of the Sikkim Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.
 - The nominees/ dependents should have lost any registered member/ worker of the due to death or the worker is permanently disabled due to an accident during the course of employment.

application_process.steps:
> **Registration Process as a Building/ Construction Worker:**

**Step 1:** The complete application form along with the required documents is required to be submitted to the Registering Officer of the area.
**Step 2:** The Registering Officer, after satisfying himself/herself with all the details, may register the worker as a beneficiary under the act and issue an Identity Card in Form XXVIII.
> **Application Process of the Welfare Scheme:**

**Step 1:** Upon receiving the Identity Card as a Building/ Construction Worker, the applicant needs to submit the application form for the concerned welfare scheme along with the mandatory documents to the Secretary or any other Officer authorized by him (self attested, if required).

Attested copy of Proof of Age.
Details of the establishment where the applicant is working.

> For the Application of the Welfare Scheme:

faqs.question: What is the age requirement for registration as a beneficiary under the Act?
faqs.answer: The building worker must be at least 18 years old and not older than 60 years old.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum service requirement to register as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Yes, the building worker must have completed 90 days of service as a building worker in the preceding 12 months.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for registering a worker as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: The Beneficiary Registering Officer is responsible for registering the worker as a beneficiary under the Act.

faqs.question: What is required for a worker to be registered as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: The worker must comply with all the requirements as laid down in the rules. Upon compliance, the Beneficiary Registering Officer will register the worker and issue an identity card with the worker's photograph affixed on it.

faqs.question: What form is used for the identity card issued to registered workers?
faqs.answer: The identity card is issued in Form XXVIII, which is annexed to these rules.

faqs.question: Is there a record of issued identity cards?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Beneficiary Registering Officer maintains a register of the issued identity cards in Form XXIX.

faqs.question: Can a worker appeal a decision made by the Beneficiary Registering Officer?
faqs.answer: Yes, any person may file an appeal to the Board within 30 days against the decision made by the Beneficiary Registering Officer. The decision of the Board is final.

faqs.question: How is the record of registered beneficiaries maintained?
faqs.answer: The Beneficiary Registering Officer maintains a district-wise register of workers registered as beneficiaries in Form XXX.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for filing a nomination?
faqs.answer: The building worker must file a nomination in Form XXXI. The nomination will be revised to include the name of the spouse upon acquiring a family or if there is any legal change in the status of the family.

faqs.question: What is required in the application for a building worker engagement certification?
faqs.answer: The application must include the employer's certificate confirming the engagement as a building worker.

faqs.question: Is there a fee associated with the application for building worker engagement certification?
faqs.answer: Yes, the application must be accompanied by documents showing payment of a registration fee of [?]20/-.

faqs.question: How often should the contribution be remitted?
faqs.answer: The contribution should be remitted once every 3 months.

faqs.question: Where should the contribution be remitted?
faqs.answer: The contribution should be remitted in any of the banks specified by the board in the district where the member resides.

faqs.question: What happens if I default on my contribution payments?
faqs.answer: If a beneficiary commits a default in the payment of contribution continuously for a period of one year, they shall cease to be a beneficiary of the fund.

faqs.question: Can I resume my membership if I have defaulted on my contributions?
faqs.answer: Yes, membership may be resumed with the permission of the Secretary of the board or any officer authorized by him. This can be done by paying the arrears of contribution, but such resumption shall not be allowed more than twice.

faqs.question: How many times can I resume my membership after defaulting?
faqs.answer: Membership resumption after defaulting is allowed a maximum of two times, with the permission of the Secretary or an authorized officer and after paying the arrears.

faqs.question: Who is entitled to the Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit under this rule?
faqs.answer: A nominee of the deceased individual is entitled for Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit.

faqs.question: To whom should the application for this benefit be submitted?
faqs.answer: The application should be submitted to the Secretary or any other Officer authorized by him.

faqs.question: What form should be used for the Permanent Disability/ Death Benefit application?
faqs.answer: The application should be made using Form XXXIV.

faqs.question: What types of situations are covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers the situations of death or permanent disability of the member.

faqs.question: Where can I obtain Form XXXIV for the application?
faqs.answer: Form XXXIV can be obtained from the Board's office or their official website: https://labour.sikkim.gov.in/Uploads/Bocw/8F1D404A-3EC3-4DA9-A4D6-75880B26D191.pdf

name: Financial Assistance To Dairy Farmers Belonging To Scheduled Tribes And Scheduled Caste For Purchase Of Basic Dairy Equipments
brief_description: The scheme aims to provide assistance to the Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Caste communities for the purchase of basic dairy equipments needed to run a small scale dairy farming, and to encourage the tribal population to adopt Animal Husbandry activities, especially Dairy Development Schemes.
details: The scheme "Financial Assistance to Dairy Farmers Belonging to Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Caste for Purchase of Basic Dairy Equipments" was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to provide assistance to the Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Caste communities for the purchase of basic dairy equipments needed to run a small scale dairy farming, and to encourage the tribal population to adopt Animal Husbandry activities, especially Dairy Development Schemes. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services. The applications for this scheme are accepted offline through the local Veterinary Officer or Assistant Director.
benefits:
##### ***Maximum Financial Assistance***

- 100% subsidy shall be provided for dairy items of general use.
- The subsidy is subject to a maximum amount of ₹30,000/- or the actual cost of the items, whichever is lower.
- The subsidy is a one-time assistance per family.

##### ***Maximum Permissible Subsidy per Item***

- Stainless Steel Cans (Twenty liters Capacity): ₹3,800/- (for 2 permissible units).
- 500 Liters Water Tanks: ₹3,500/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Calf Nipple Bucket: ₹1,500/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Spray Pump 15 Liters Capacity: ₹2,000/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Steel Buckets: ₹2,200/- (for 2 permissible units).
- 0.5 Horsepower water Pump: ₹5,000/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Ceiling Fans: ₹4,000/- (for 2 permissible units).
- Steel Vessels 5 Liters Capacity: ₹900/- (for 2 permissible units).
- Spade: ₹250/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Grooming Brush: ₹400/- (for 2 permissible units).
- Gamelas: ₹500/- (for 2 permissible units).
- Nylon Rope: ₹400/- (for 2.5 kilograms).
- Sickle: ₹250/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Pickaxe: ₹300/- (for 1 permissible unit).
- Rubber mat: ₹5,000/- (for 2 permissible units).

##### ***Benefit Disbursal***

- Subsidy shall be directly credited to the beneficiary’s bank account.
- In case of limited purchase of dairy items, proportionate subsidy shall be released.
- The Department will release the subsidy within 60 days of receiving the documents completed in all respects.

##### ***Conditions***

- The beneficiary must use the dairy equipments purchased for the development of their dairy unit.
- The beneficiary shall abide by the provision of the said scheme, and undertake to comply with the Pattern of Assistance of the scheme as contained in the scheme.
- The beneficiary must use the dairy equipments for a minimum period of 3 (three) years from the date of purchase, subject to normal wear and tear.
- The beneficiary solemnly undertakes to refund the cost of the items if the items are found misutilised or missing.
- In case of breach of any clause, the Government is free to recover the subsidy released through any due benefits under other eligible schemes of the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services and/or under the land revenue code.
exclusions:
- The applicant must not have availed subsidy under any scheme of the Government of Goa for any of the equipments applied under this scheme.
- The subsidy under this scheme is a one-time assistance per family, implying that prior availment by a family member excludes the applicant.
eligibility:
- The applicant must be a resident of Goa for at least five preceding years.
- The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Tribe or Scheduled Caste Community.
- The applicant must be a Dairy Farmer.
- The applicant must have at least two milch animals.
- The two milch animals must be Local Cows, Indigenous cows, Cross Bred cows, Local Buffaloes, or Improved Buffaloes.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should take a printout of the [prescribed proforma](https://ahvs.goa.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/financial-assistance-Dairy-equipment.pdf).
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents, within the prescribed period (if any), to the local **Veterinary Officer or Assistant Director**. 
**Step 4:** The concerned local Veterinary Officer or Assistant Director shall scrutinize the application and verify the documents to ensure they are complete in all respects. The officer must then forward the application to the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services, Patto-Panaji, along with his or her recommendation, within 15 days of its receipt.
**Step 5:** The application will undergo further processing at the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services. The application will be approved by the Directorate if it is found to be in order based on the established scheme provisions.

##### ***Post-Approval Processes***
**Step 1:** On approval of the application, the beneficiary must purchase the dairy equipment. The beneficiary must then submit the original purchase receipts or bills to the local Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer, within 90 days of the application approval.
**Step 2:** The bills will be verified by the concerned officer. Certification of the bills will be done only after an inspection of the purchased equipment has been carried out. The verified and certified documents are then submitted to the Head Office for the release of the subsidy amount.
**Step 3:** On receiving the documents completed in all respects, the Department will release the approved subsidy. The subsidy will be released within 60 days of the completed documents being received and shall be directly credited to the beneficiary’s bank account.

documents_required: Caste Certificate Issued by Competent Authority.
Aadhar Consent Form Duly Filled In.
Two Passport Size Photographs of the Applicant.
Prescribed Affidavit Duly Notarised (Used to declare non-availment of subsidy under any Government scheme for the applied items).
Information of Existing Milch Animals (Details of Cross Bred Cow/Improved She Buffalo, Local/Non-Descript Adult Heifers, and Young Female Calves) (Required on the application form).
Original Purchase Receipts or Bills (Must be submitted within 90 days of application approval).

faqs.question: What specific community criteria must be fulfilled by the applicant to be considered eligible for this financial assistance program?
faqs.answer: The applicant must belong to either the Scheduled Tribes Community or the Scheduled Caste Community to qualify for this particular scheme.

faqs.question: Following the approval of the initial application, what is the required timeframe for the beneficiary to submit the original purchase documents for the equipment?
faqs.answer: After the application is approved, the beneficiary is mandated to submit the original purchase receipts or bills to the local Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer within 90 days.

faqs.question: For how long is an applicant required to have maintained continuous residency within the state of Goa prior to submitting their application?
faqs.answer: Applicants must demonstrate that they have been a resident of the state of Goa for a minimum of 5 preceding years immediately before applying.

faqs.question: If the procured items are later discovered to be missing or utilized for purposes other than the intended dairy development, what are the financial consequences?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary provides a solemn undertaking to refund the full cost of the items if they are subsequently found to be either misutilised or completely missing during verification.

faqs.question: What specific rules or guidelines must the beneficiary agree to adhere to once the grant of subsidy has been officially provided by the Government?
faqs.answer: In consideration of the subsidy grant, the beneficiary shall abide by all the provisions of the scheme and comply fully with the stipulated Pattern of Assistance.

faqs.question: What is the minimum mandatory number of milch animals an applicant must own, and what types of animals satisfy this requirement?
faqs.answer: The applicant must possess at least 2 milch animals. These can be Local Cows, Indigenous cows, Cross Bred cows, Local Buffaloes, or Improved Buffaloes.

faqs.question: If I have previously received governmental support for dairy equipment, does that prevent me from receiving assistance for new items under this program?
faqs.answer: The applicant must not have availed subsidy under any scheme of the Government of Goa for the specific equipments for which they are currently applying.

faqs.question: Is there a mandatory length of time the beneficiary must commit to keeping and actively using the subsidized dairy equipments?
faqs.answer: Yes, the beneficiary is required to use the dairy equipments for a minimum period of 3 (three) years from the date of purchase, accounting for normal wear and tear.

faqs.question: Once all required documentation, including purchase bills, has been verified and found complete, how long will it take for the subsidy to be released?
faqs.answer: The Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services will release the approved subsidy directly to the beneficiary’s bank account within 60 days of receiving all completed documents.

faqs.question: What is the highest total financial support I can expect to receive under this assistance program for purchasing necessary dairy equipment?
faqs.answer: A 100% subsidy shall be provided for dairy items, subject to a maximum amount of ₹30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand only) or the actual cost of the items, whichever amount is lower.

faqs.question: Are there any processing charges or monetary fees associated with the preparation and official submission of the application form for this assistance?
faqs.answer: No processing fee or monetary charges shall be levied or collected from the applicant for the submission of the application under this scheme.

faqs.question: Through which specific local government officials or offices should the completed application form and all supporting documents be submitted?
faqs.answer: Applications must be submitted in duplicate through the local Veterinary Officer or the Assistant Director of the Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services.

faqs.question: If I breach any of the scheme's clauses, how is the Government authorized to recover the released subsidy amount from me?
faqs.answer: In the event of a breach, the Government is free to recover the subsidy through any due benefits under other eligible schemes of the Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services or under the land revenue code.

faqs.question: After receiving the financial assistance and purchasing the items, what is the primary purpose for which the dairy equipment must be utilized?
faqs.answer: The applicant solemnly undertakes to use the purchased dairy equipments exclusively for the purpose of the development and operation of their dairy unit.

name: Reimbursement of Tution Fee for SC/ST/OBC/Min students in Public Schools in Class I to XII
brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial support by reimbursing tuition and compulsory fees for SC/ST/OBC students from low-income families (below ₹3,00,000/- per annum) studying in recognized schools in Delhi. Beneficiaries must meet academic and attendance criteria.
details: The scheme "Reimbursement of Tuition Fees for SC/ST/OBC Categories Students Studying in Class I to XII" by the Department for the Welfare of SC/ST/OBC/Minorities, Government of NCT of Delhi aims to provide financial assistance by reimbursing tuition and other compulsory fees for eligible students from SC/ST/OBC categories studying in recognized public schools in Delhi. The scheme ensures that students with a family income below ₹3,00,000/- per annum receive reimbursement for tuition, lab, and library fees, subject to academic performance and attendance criteria. Eligible students must be enrolled in classes 1st to 12th in schools recognized by the Department of Education, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, or municipal local bodies of Delhi.
benefits:
**Reimbursement Amount:** Maximum reimbursement of ₹48,000/- or actual paid fees (whichever is less) covering tuition, lab, and library fees.
**Conditions for Disbursement**

- Student must score 50% and above marks in the preceding year.
- Student must have at least 70% attendance in the preceding year.

**Mode of Disbursement:** Direct transfer to the student’s bank account (joint account with parent/guardian allowed).
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a Student.
1. The applicant should be studying in Class 1st to 12th.
1. The applicant should be enrolled in a school recognized/affiliated with the Dept. of Education, GNCTD or Municipal Local Bodies of Delhi.
1. The applicant should have scored 50% or above in the previous academic year.
1. The applicant should have at least 80% attendance in the preceding year.
1. The applicant should not be repeating the same class.
1. The annual income of the family of the applicant should not exceed ₹2,00,000/-.

application_process.steps:
> **Registration**

**Step 1:** Visit the [e-District Portal](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/) of the Govt. of NCT of Delhi.
**Step 2:** On the top right corner of the homepage, click “[Login/Register](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/Account/Login)”, then click “[Register](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/in/en/Account/Register.html)". You will be taken to the "Citizen Registration Form". Carefully read the “Guidelines for Online Registration” provided at the bottom of the page.
**Step 3:** In the Citizen Registration Form, select "Aadhaar Card" as the Document Type, and provide the Aadhaar Number. Fill in the captcha code and click “Continue”. 
**Step 4:** On the next page, fill in all the mandatory fields. If required, verify your Email ID and Mobile Number via OTP. Enter the Captcha code and click “Continue to Register”. You will receive your Login ID and Password on the Mobile Number/Email Address provided during the registration.
> **Application**

**Step 1:** Visit the [e-District Portal](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/) of the Govt. of NCT of Delhi.
**Step 2:** On the top right corner of the homepage, click “[Login/Register](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/Account/Login)”, you will be taken to the “Citizen Login Form”
**Step 3:** Provide your Login ID and Password, enter the Captcha code and click “Login”.
**Step 4:** Go to the home page and click “Apply Service”. Navigate to the scheme that you intend to apply for. Click on the name of the scheme. You will be taken to the scheme's online application form.
**Step 5:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size. Carefully review all the information provided and the documents uploaded. Make any necessary corrections. Acknowledge and agree to the terms and conditions and/or declaration (if any), then click "Finish”. 
**Step 6:** An OTP will be received on the registered mobile number. Provide the OTP and click “Submit”. An acknowledgement of successful submission shall be sent over Email/SMS/Both.
> **Track Application Status**

**Step 1:** Visit the "[Track Your Application](https://edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in/Public/TrackApplication)" page.
**Step 2:** Fill in all the mandatory fields. Enter the Captcha Code, and click "Submit".
Your current application status will be displayed.

documents_required: Attendance Record of the Previous Year.
Income Certificate (issued by a competent authority of Delhi).
Caste Certificate, issued in the student’s name or father’s name by SDM/Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), GNCTD.
Original Fee Receipt for the current academic session.
Bank Account Details (student’s name/joint account with parent/guardian, Aadhaar-seeded).

faqs.question: What is the maximum annual family income allowed for applicants under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The family income must not exceed ₹3,00,000/- per annum, and a valid income certificate from a Delhi authority is required.

faqs.question: Which categories of students are eligible for fee reimbursement under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC) are eligible for this benefit.

faqs.question: What type of schools are covered under this fee reimbursement scheme?
faqs.answer: Only students studying in schools recognized by the Department of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, or municipal local bodies of Delhi are eligible.

faqs.question: Is there any academic performance requirement for students to avail this benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, students must have scored at least 50% marks in the preceding academic year to qualify for fee reimbursement.

faqs.question: What is the minimum attendance requirement for students to be eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Students must have a minimum of 70% attendance in the preceding academic year to be considered for reimbursement.

faqs.question: Are students repeating the same class eligible for fee reimbursement?
faqs.answer: No, students who are repeating the same class are not eligible for any benefits under this scheme.

faqs.question: What is the maximum amount that can be reimbursed under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The maximum reimbursement amount is ₹48,000/- per year or the actual fees paid, whichever is lower.

faqs.question: Which fees are covered under the reimbursement scheme?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees, lab fees, and library fees are covered under this reimbursement scheme.

faqs.question: What documents are required to prove the student’s caste category?
faqs.answer: A caste certificate issued by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) or Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Government of NCT of Delhi, is mandatory.

faqs.question: What should be done if the caste certificate is not issued by Delhi authorities?
faqs.answer: If the caste certificate is not issued by Delhi authorities, a domicile certificate of Delhi must be submitted.

faqs.question: Is a joint bank account acceptable for receiving reimbursement under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, a joint bank account in the student’s name along with a parent or guardian is permissible.

faqs.question: What is the requirement regarding the student’s bank account for reimbursement?
faqs.answer: The bank account must be active and linked with the student’s Aadhaar number for direct transfer of funds.

faqs.question: What proof of fee payment is required for reimbursement?
faqs.answer: Original fee receipts for the current academic session must be uploaded on the portal during application.

faqs.question: Where can students register to apply for this reimbursement scheme?
faqs.answer: Students must register on the e-District Portal of the Government of NCT of Delhi to apply.

name: Nirman Shramik Kalyan Yojana
nodal_department: Labour and Employees State Insurance Department
department: Labour And Employee's State Insurance Department, Odisha
brief_description: The scheme “Nirman Shramik Kalyan Yojana” was launched by the Labour and Employee's State Insurance Department, Government of Odisha. name: Kalakar Kritadnyata Nidhi: Incentive for Self Employment
brief_description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance not exceeding ₹50,000/- or the actual cost, whichever is less, to needy Goan artists or their families for setting up self-employment ventures, helping them establish sustainable income sources. The applications for this scheme are accepted Offline.
details: The scheme "Kalakar Kritadnyata Nidhi" was launched by the Directorate of Art & Culture, Government of Goa. The "Incentive for Self-Employment" component of the scheme aims to provide financial assistance not exceeding ₹50,000/- or the actual cost, whichever is less, to needy Goan artists or their families for setting up self-employment ventures, helping them establish sustainable income sources. The applications for this scheme are accepted Offline.
benefits:
> ***Financial Assistance***

- ₹50,000/- or the actual cost, whichever is less, shall be provided for setting up self employment venture.
- The financial assistance amount shall be disbursed to the eligible applicant in the form of Electronic Clearing System mode.
- The assistance is provided as a one-time grant.

> ***Conditions***

- The details of the expenditure incurred along with the vouchers must be furnished to the department after utilizing the grant.
- The unutilized amount out of the sanctioned amount, if any, shall be refunded to the Government within the stipulated timeframe.
exclusions: Individuals who have already availed self-employment benefits earlier under any Government scheme, Autonomous bodies, or Corporations are not eligible.
eligibility:
- The applicant must be Goan, i.e., born and brought up in Goa.
- The artist must be an artist recognized by the Directorate of Art & Culture, Government of Goa.
- The income of the family of the applicant (from all sources) must not exceed ₹2,00,000/- per annum.
- The applicant must not be less than 50 years in age. (The Government may relax the age criteria for deserving cases under special circumstances.)
- The applicant must not be employed or self-employed at the time of application.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** Visit the office of the Directorate of Art & Culture, Sanskruti Bhavan, Patto, Panaji, Goa, and collect the prescribed application form for the scheme.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the completed application form along with all required documents directly to the ***Directorate of Art & Culture, Sanskruti Bhavan, Patto, Panaji, Goa.***

##### ***Post-Application Processes***
**Step 1:** The Directorate shall forward the application to the sub-committee for scrutinizing the application thoroughly. The Director shall give its recommendations to the sub-committee.
**Step 2:** The sub-committee shall consider the received applications and recommend the names of the artists which are considered fit by the sub-committee to avail the benefits under this scheme. The committee shall decide the quantum of assistance to be released to the needy artist.
**Step 3:** After the committee decides on the quantum of assistance, the approval from the Government shall be obtained for disbursement of the financial assistance.
**Step 4:** After obtaining Government approval, the Director shall disburse the one-time financial assistance amount to the eligible applicant in the form of Electronic Clearing System mode to the bank account.

documents_required: Certificate From Any Gazetted Officer (confirming that the applicant is not employed or self employed).
Estimate Indicating The Cost Of The Self Employment Venture (from competent authority).
Documentary Proof Of Recognition By The Directorate Of Art & Culture, Government Of Goa.
Declaration Or Affidavit (confirming that the applicant has not availed self employment benefits earlier under any Government scheme, Autonomous bodies, or Corporations).
Details Of The Expenditure Incurred Along With The Vouchers (to be furnished to the department after utilizing the grant).

faqs.question: What is the maximum amount of financial assistance that can be provided to an artist or their family member for establishing a self employment venture?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance not exceeding ₹50,000/- or the actual cost, whichever is less, shall be provided for setting up a self employment venture.

faqs.question: If I am currently working in a private company on a regular basis, am I eligible to apply for financial assistance under this component?
faqs.answer: No, the applicant must not be employed or self employed at the time of application. A certificate from any Gazetted Officer confirming non-employment status must be submitted.

faqs.question: What happens if I have previously received self employment benefits from any other government scheme or autonomous body? Can I still apply for this assistance?
faqs.answer: No, those applicants who have not availed self employment benefits earlier under any Government scheme, Autonomous bodies, or Corporations shall only be eligible for the financial assistance under this incentive.

faqs.question: Is there any specific age requirement that needs to be fulfilled by the artist applying for self employment financial assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be not less than 50 years of age. However, the Government may relax the age criteria for deserving cases under special circumstances.

faqs.question: What is the maximum annual family income limit from all sources that an applicant must maintain to be eligible for this financial assistance?
faqs.answer: The applicant must have an annual family income from all sources that does not exceed ₹2,00,000/- per annum to be eligible for this component.

faqs.question: What kind of documentary evidence regarding the cost of the self employment venture needs to be submitted along with the application?
faqs.answer: An estimate indicating the cost of the self employment venture from a competent authority must be submitted along with the application.

faqs.question: Do I need to be officially recognized as an artist by any government department to be eligible for applying under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be recognized by the Directorate of Art & Culture, Government of Goa. Documentary proof of this recognition must be submitted with the application.

faqs.question: After receiving the financial assistance, what are the reporting requirements regarding how the funds were utilized for the self employment venture?
faqs.answer: The details of the expenditure incurred along with the vouchers must be furnished to the department after utilizing the grant for the self employment venture.

faqs.question: If I do not utilize the entire sanctioned amount for my self employment venture, what should I do with the remaining funds?
faqs.answer: The unutilized amount out of the sanctioned amount, if any, shall be refunded to the Government within the stipulated timeframe as specified in the guidelines.

faqs.question: Through which mode will the financial assistance amount be transferred to the beneficiary's account once the application is approved by the authorities?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance amount shall be disbursed to the eligible applicant in the form of Electronic Clearing System mode directly to the bank account.

faqs.question: Where should I submit my application form and all the required documents to apply for this self employment financial assistance?
faqs.answer: The application must be submitted directly to the Directorate of Art & Culture, Sanskruti Bhavan, Patto, Panaji, Goa during working days at the office of the department.

faqs.question: Is there any certificate required to prove that I am not currently employed or engaged in any self employment activity?
faqs.answer: Yes, a certificate to the effect that the applicant is not employed or is not self employed from any Gazetted Officer must be enclosed to the application.

name: Innovation In Science Pursuit For Inspired Research (INSPIRE) - Faculty Fellowship
brief_description: The "INSPIRE FACULTY FELLOWSHIP" component provides opportunities to 100 persons every year with Ph.D. qualifications in the age group of 27-32 years for 5 years to carry out research in both basic and applied science areas including engineering, medicine, agriculture, and veterinary sciences.
details:
The "INSPIRE FACULTY FELLOWSHIP" component provides opportunities to 100 persons every year with Ph.D. qualifications in the age group of 27-32 years for 5 years to carry out research in both basic and applied science areas including engineering, medicine, agriculture, and veterinary sciences for establishing themselves as independent researchers. It grants an attractive fellowship for a duration of 5 years. The objective of the scheme is to encourage young researchers to continue research in areas of S&T, Medicine, Agriculture, Pharmacy, and Veterinary Sciences.
Purpose
1. To provide attractive opportunities for young achievers for developing independent scientific profiles and launch them toward fulfilling long-term careers.
2. To augment high-quality scientific manpower in scientific and educational institutions, especially the Central and State universities.
3. While vertical migration from the other INSPIRE components would be encouraged, the faculty fellowship component also provides the opportunity to meritorious candidates for lateral entry into INSPIRE scheme.
4. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship provides an opportunity to post-doctoral fellows for carrying out independent research however does not guarantee a regular position after 5 years.
benefits:
> **Amount**

1. Each selected INSPIRE Faculty Fellow will be eligible to receive a consolidated amount of ₹1,25,000/- per month as a fellowship with an annual increment of ₹2,000/-. 
1. In addition, a Research Grant of ₹7,00,000 every year for 5 years will also be provided to each successful candidate including the carry-forward amount, if any, from the previous year. 
1. The consolidated amount of ₹1,25,000/- per month is an all-inclusive fellowship and taxable as per the Indian IT Act.

> **Duration**

1. The INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship is for a maximum period of 5 (five) years.
exclusions: No Fellow shall avail of two fellowships concurrently during the tenure of this Fellowship period.
eligibility:
> **Essential**

1. Indian citizens and People of Indian origin with PIO status having Ph.D. degrees (in science, mathematics, engineering, pharmacy, medicine, and agriculture-related subjects) from any recognized university in the world.
1. Candidates should possess a minimum of 60% (or equivalent CGPA) marks throughout their academic profile starting from the Senior Secondary Examination (Class 12 onwards).
1. Those that have submitted their Ph.D. theses and are awaiting the award of their degree shall also be eligible. However, selection for the Fellowship will be confirmed only after the Ph.D. degree is awarded.
1. The upper age limit as of 1st January of the respective year of advertisement, is 32 years for General Category. However, for SC, ST, and Women candidates, the upper age limit will be 37 years. For persons with benchmark disabilities (Divyangjan with not less than 40 percent of a specified disability), the upper age limit will be 42 years.
1. Publication(s) in highly reputed journals demonstrating the outstanding research potential of the candidate.
1. Candidates who are employed in regular/contractual positions within India may also apply for INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship for improvement and enhancement in their career prospects but, upon selection, the candidates will need to resign (no lien or deputation or any type of leave would be accepted) from the current job and organization before taking up the INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship. 
1. Candidates, who get selected for regular positions in any institute/university after submission of the IFF application, would be entitled to receive the Research Grant only as INSPIRE Faculty Fellows.

> **Desirable**

1. Candidates who are within the top 1% in Class 12 examination, IIT-JEE rank holders, 1st rank holders either in graduation or post-graduation level university examinations.

application_process.steps:
> **Mode of Application**

1. Eligible candidates need to submit applications ONLINE through the portal of INSPIRE program only. No other mode of submission of the application is permitted.
1. To apply ONLINE, please visit the [website ](https://online-inspire.gov.in)and follow the process described therein. After the successful submission of the application online, the candidate may obtain a printout of the application and keep it for his/her personal reference.
> **Method of Selection**

1. The Indian National Science Academy (INSA), New Delhi, in coordination with DST, is implementing this INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship Scheme up to the stage of recommendation of candidates for INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship.
1. A three-tier selection process, viz. evaluation by discipline-based Expert Committees, followed by the recommendations of the Apex Level Committee and INSPIRE Faculty Award Council. Based on the recommendations of these Committees, DST makes the final selection.

Proof of Academic Qualifications (Degree / Passing Certificate / Marksheets) (from class 12th standard onwards)
Community/Caste Certificate (only if the applicant belongs to SC/ST)

Details of Professional Recognitions, Awards, and Fellowships received

Methodology and Workplan are also to be submitted online in .pdf format if required.

Every Faculty Fellow needs to provide budget estimates with year-wise detailed break-up under various Heads such as manpower cost, consumables including chemicals, travel, contingency, overhead costs, etc. and non-recurring cost such as equipment for utilization of the Research Grant to the DST-INSPIRE Programme Division along with joining documents.
To settle the Faculty Fellowship grant upon completion/resignation, INSPIRE Faculty Fellow shall upload all necessary documents in his/her INSPIRE Web-Portal account such as:

Performance Report in the prescribed format.

Unspent balance if any (unspent balance and other earnings against the released grant (if any), shall be remitted to the Consolidated Fund of India (through Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP) i.e., https://www.bharatkosh.gov.in. and the copy of the same is to be uploaded to the portal.
> Transfer or Change of Host Institution (including absorption)
The Faculty Fellow needs to inform the DST-INSPIRE Programme Division immediately with the following documents to effect the change and smooth facilitation of the transfer of funds etc.
Appointment Letter of permanent employment or justification for a change of Host Institution.
NOC from the present Host Institute and Acceptance Letter from the new Host Institute.
Joining Letter from the new Host Institute due to transfer or permanent employment (either the same or a different Host Institution),
Fresh signed copy of the Undertaking (not required in case of permanent employment in the same Host Institution),
Up-to-date financial documents from the present Host Institute (also in case of permanent employment in the same Host Institute).

According to Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), “adoption is a process by which a child who is abandoned/separated from biological parents, becomes the legitimate.
details: The scheme "Child Adoption - Tamil Nadu" was launched by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu. The scheme aims to provide a family for orphaned, abandoned, destitute and neglected children. According to Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), “adoption is a process by which a child who is abandoned / separated from biological parents, becomes the legitimate child of a new set of parents referred to as adoptive parents, with all the rights, privileges and responsibilities that are attached to this relationship”.
benefits:
- Accommodation, food, and health care to the babies till they are given in adoption.
- A family to the destitute child and a child to childless parents.

> **Special concessions are given to female government employees to adopt children:**

- Special adoption leave of 270 days is extended to female government servants of the state government who adopt a child below one year. The leave is eligible only from the date of legalization of adoption.
eligibility:
1. The parents must have at least two years of a stable marital relationship.
1. The single prospective adoptive parents should be between 30-55 years of age. 
1. An unmarried/single male persons are not eligible to adopt a girl child.
1. The parents should have adequate financial resources to upbring the child.
1. Age Criteria:

 - **For a child up to 4 years old:**

 1. Maximum composite age of the Prospective Adoptive Parents: 90 years.
 1. For a single Prospective Adoptive Parent: Minimum age 25 years, maximum age 45 years.

 - **For a child above 4 years up to 8 years old:**

 1. Maximum composite age of the Prospective Adoptive Parents: 100 years.
 1. For a single Prospective Adoptive Parent: Minimum age 25 years, maximum age 50 years.

 - **For a child above 8 years up to 18 years old:**

 1. Maximum composite age of the Prospective Adoptive Parents: 110 years.
 1. For a single Prospective Adoptive Parent: Minimum age 25 years, maximum age 55 years.

application_process.steps:
**Step 1:** The interested applicant should visit (during office hours) the office State Adoption Resource Agency/Directorate of Social Defence/Concerned Probation Officer and request a hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the concerned staff.
**Step 2:** In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
**Step 3:** Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the State Adoption Resource Agency/Directorate of Social Defence/Concerned Probation Officer. 
**Step 4:** Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, and a unique identification number (if applicable).

documents_required: Proof of Residence (Aadhaar Card/Voter ID card/Passport /Driving License/ Electricity Card).
Proof of Income of Last Year (Pay Bill/ Income Tax Certificate).
Copy of Birth Certificate of the Prospective Adoptive Parents.

faqs.question: What kind of assistance is provided to children under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides accommodation, food, and healthcare to the babies until they are adopted, and also facilitates the process of providing a family to the destitute child and a child to childless parents.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for prospective adoptive parents?
faqs.answer: Prospective Adoptive Parents must have a stable marital relationship of at least two years. Age and marital status criteria vary depending on the age of the child to be adopted.

faqs.question: What is the definition of child adoption according to CARA?
faqs.answer: According to the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), adoption is a process by which a child who is abandoned or separated from biological parents becomes the legitimate child of a new set of parents (adoptive parents), with all the rights, privileges, and responsibilities attached to this relationship.

faqs.question: Which legal acts govern the process of adoption in India?
faqs.answer: The Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 (HAMA) and the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 govern adoption.

faqs.question: How is the child adoption process regulated?
faqs.answer: The adoption process is regulated by Non-Governmental Organisations and involves various authorities and agencies to ensure a thorough and legal process.

faqs.question: How many institutions are involved in implementing the adoption scheme?
faqs.answer: There are 23 institutions involved in implementing the adoption scheme.

faqs.question: Who should be contacted for information about adoption?
faqs.answer: Contact the State Adoption Resource Agency, the Directorate of Social Defence in Chennai, the concerned Probation Officer, or the 23 Licensed Specialized Adoption Agencies.

faqs.question: What documents need to be submitted for adoption?
faqs.answer: Documents include PAN Card/Passport, Proof of Residence, Proof of Income, Marriage Certificate and Photograph, Birth Certificate of the Prospective Adoptive Parents, Medical Certificate, and a Letter of identification from friends or relatives.

faqs.question: What happens if a prospective adoptive parent is found ineligible after submission of documents?
faqs.answer: If found ineligible, the prospective adoptive parent(s) will not be allowed to proceed with the adoption process and will be informed accordingly.

faqs.question: Are single males allowed to adopt a girl child?
faqs.answer: No, an unmarried or single male person is not eligible to adopt a girl child.

name: Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition
nodal_department: Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department
brief_description: The scheme “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” by the Department of Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities aims to promote physical fitness and competitive spirit among citizens through a state-level stair-climbing competition on Mount Girnar, offering cash prizes to the top 10 winners.
details: The scheme “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” by the Department of Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities, Government of Gujarat, aims to encourage physical endurance, sports participation, and cultural spirit among individuals by organizing an annual state-level stair-climbing competition on Mount Girnar. Out of the 9,900 steps of the mountain, the competition mandates male participants to complete 5,500 steps and female participants to complete 2,200 steps. Participants who secure positions among the top 10 are rewarded with substantial cash prizes, thereby motivating individuals of all backgrounds to embrace physical challenges and celebrate Gujarat’s heritage.
benefits: - **Cash Prize:** A total of ₹8,40,000/- is distributed among the first 10 winners.
eligibility:

 - The applicant should be physically fit and willing to participate in the stair-climbing competition.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to participate in the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition”?

faqs.answer: Yes, the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” mandates that male participants must climb 5,500 steps, whereas female participants are required to complete 2,200 steps as part of the competition.

faqs.question: What type of benefit is provided to the winners?
faqs.answer: The winners of the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” are awarded a cumulative cash prize of ₹8,40,000/- which is distributed among the top 10 performing participants based on their competition results.

faqs.question: How many winners are selected in the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition”?

faqs.question: Is there any age restriction to participate in the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition”?
faqs.answer: The official scheme guidelines for the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” do not specify any age restriction; however, it is expected that the participant should be physically capable of climbing the steps of Mount Girnar as per the competition requirements.

faqs.question: Is there any reservation or special quota for any group in the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition”?
faqs.answer: The scheme guidelines for the “Girnar Arohan-Avrohan Competition” do not mention any reservation, quota, or special preference for any particular group; participation is open to all eligible individuals.

name: Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Degree)
department: All India Council For Technical Education (AICTE)
brief_description: A scholarship scheme by MoE for Girl Students admitted in 1st or 2nd Year of the technical degree course in an AICTE approved institution. The benefits are provided for max. 4 years for first-year admitted students and max. 3 years for second-year admitted students through lateral entry.
details: A scholarship scheme by AICTE, MoE for Girl Students admitted in 1st or 2nd Year of the technical degree course in an AICTE approved institution. A maximum of two girl children per family are eligible to avail of the benefits. The benefits are provided for a period of maximum of 4 years for first-year admitted students and a maximum of 3 years for second-year admitted students through lateral entry. This scheme is an attempt to give young women the opportunity to further their education and prepare for a successful future by empowering Women through knowledge, skill, and self-confidence.
benefits: **₹ 50,000/- per annum** for every year of study, i.e. maximum of 4 years for first-year admitted students and a maximum of 3 years for second-year admitted students, through lateral entry as a lump sum amount towards payment of **college fees, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipment, software**, etc.
exclusions:
1. If a candidate failed/drops out in a subsequent year, she will not be eligible for further scholarship.
 1. If it is found that the student is in receipt of financial assistance in the shape of scholarship/any emoluments, salary, stipend, etc. from any other source during her course of study in the institute, the scholarship shall be discontinued.
 1. If the gap period between the year of passing the qualifying examination and the admission session in a degree course is more than two years.
 1. The scholarship is only applicable to a **maximum of two girl children of a family**.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a **Girl Student.**1. The applicant must be pursuing either **the First year of the degree course** OR **the Second year of the Degree course through lateral entry.**1. The **annual income of the family** (from all sources) must not be more than **₹ 8,00,000/- per annum** during the current financial year.1. **All eligible girls** (who submit online scholarship form) **from the following 13 Union Territories and North Eastern States** i.e. Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UT), Jammu and Kashmir (UT), Ladakh (UT), Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu (UT), Lakshadweep (UT), Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim & Tripura will be given a scholarship by AICTE.

##### ***Registration Process***
##### **Step 1:****** ***Registration and Profile Creation***
Visit the [PIPDIC website.](https://pipdic.in/,) Click "Login". Click the “New customer” link under the “Login” menu, enter a username, email-id, password, and captcha, and then click the "Register" button.
##### **Step 2:****** ***Email Verification and Login***

- Use the registered email-id to log in. An OTP is sent to the registered email address.
- The applicant is then required to enter the OTP and click "Login" to access to the customer dashboard.

##### **Step 3:****** ***Profile Update***

- Upon successful login, the customer needs to update their profile by accessing the "Edit Profile" option (top right corner of the dashboard).
- The applicant must provide all required details. Click "Submit".

##### ***Application Process (Loan Application)***
##### **Step 1:****** ***Accessing the Loan Application Form***

- To initiate the loan application process, the applicant must navigate from the customer dashboard by clicking on the "Applications" tab.

##### **Step 2:****** ***Reviewing Checklist and Accepting Terms***

- A pop-up window displaying a checklist of General Terms and Conditions, interest rate structure, investigation fees, and collateral security norms will appear for review.
- Carefully read this checklist, confirm that all necessary documents have been gathered as requested, and click the “I Agree” button to proceed to the application form.

##### **Step 3:****** ***Filling the Loan Application Form***
Fill the multi-step application form, providing appropriate details in all mandatory fields across the required steps.
##### **Step 4:****** ***Declaration and Submission***
The applicant must carefully read and agree to the comprehensive declaration provided within the application form (covering confirmation of true information, absence of unauthorized borrowing arrangements, and consent to verification) before finally ticking the "I agree to terms" checkbox and clicking the final "Submit" button for the main application form.
##### **Step 5:****** ***Promoter Bio-Data and Document Upload***
The system will redirect the applicant to enter the Biodata of the Promoter, Partner, or Director, which is typically a multi-step process. The necessary KYC and supporting documents must be uploaded by clicking the "Choose File" button next to each field.
##### **Step 6:****** ***Application Fees Payment***

- Once the entire application and bio-data submission is complete, pay the applicable application fee.

- If selecting online payment, the system automatically redirects the applicant to the payment summary page, where they verify their details and make the payment.

##### **Step 7:****** ***Receiving and Saving Payment Receipt***

- Upon successful payment, the user is redirected back to PIPDIC website, where a receipt for the application fee paid is generated.
- The applicant can print this receipt or save it to their computer as a PDF for future reference.

##### ***Application Status Tracking and Support***
The customer can monitor the status of their submitted application (which will initially show a status like 'UNDER REVIEW') by clicking the "View My application" link on the dashboard and selecting the relevant loan application in the drop-down menu.
##### ***Application Fees***

- For loans up to ₹25,00,000/-, the application fee is ₹100/-.
- For loans above ₹25,00,000/-, the application fee is ₹200/-.

##### ***Grievance Redressal / Help & Support***

- The applicant can contact the Managing Director, Pondicherry Industrial Promotion Development and Investment Corporation Limited at No.60, Romain Rolland Street, Puducherry 605001.
- The office phone number is 0413-2334361.
- The email address for contact is info@pipdic.com.
- The General Manager (Administration) can be contacted via mobile at 9894653835.

details: Launched in 1981, the scheme “Distribution of Free House Sites to Scheduled Caste/Other Economically Backward Classes” by the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department, Government of Puducherry was introduced to distribute free house sites to Scheduled Caste and Other Economically Backward Classes. Through this scheme, the homeless poor Scheduled Caste people, and other Economically backward class people, who meet the eligibility criteria, are provided housing sites to enable them to construct their own houses. name: Gagan Bharari Shiksha Yojana for OBC (Dhangar) Students
brief_description: The scheme "Gagan Bharari Shiksha Yojana for OBC (Dhangar) Students" by the Directorate of Social Welfare, Government of Goa aims to provide additional financial assistance to OBC (Dhangar) students to supplement their Post Matric Scholarship maintenance allowance.
details: The scheme "Gagan Bharari Shiksha Yojana for OBC (Dhangar) Students" by the Directorate of Social Welfare, Government of Goa aims to provide additional financial assistance to OBC (Dhangar) students to supplement their Post Matric Scholarship maintenance allowance. Through this scheme, additional monthly allowances are provided to OBC (Dhangar) students to meet their food, travel, and disability-related expenses, as the existing Post Matric Scholarship amounts are inadequate. The applications for this scheme are accepted online. The scheme is being implemented by the Chief Minister Scholarship Portal, Government of Goa.
benefits:
**Additional Maintenance Allowance**

- Day Scholars: ₹750 per month
- Hostel Residents: ₹1,500 per month

**Duration:** 10 months during the academic year

**Additional Disability Allowance**
Amount: ₹750 per month
**Duration:** 10 months during the academic year
eligibility:
- The applicant should be a Student. 
- The applicant should belong to the OBC (Dhangar) community.
- The applicant should have availed (or be eligible for) the Centrally Sponsored Post Matric Scholarship during the current academic year.

name: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin, Uttarakhand
brief_description: The scheme aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible rural households in Uttarakhand, ensuring dignified living conditions for economically and socially disadvantaged families.
details: The “Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin” is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Department of Rural Development, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible rural households in Uttarakhand, ensuring dignified living conditions for economically and socially disadvantaged families.
benefits: Under this scheme, selected eligible beneficiaries receive financial assistance of ₹130,000/- for house construction. Beneficiaries are also provided ₹12,000/- for toilet construction under convergence with MGNREGA/Swajal, along with 95 man-days of labour employment from MGNREGA. After the house is completed, the State Government provides an additional ₹6,000/- for purchasing kitchen utensils as per the Hon’ble Chief Minister’s announcement.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The selection of eligible beneficiaries for housing is done based on the “Social, Economic and Caste Census 2011 (SECC-2011)” and the Awaas Plus Permanent Waiting List.

application_process.steps:
- There is no provision for submitting a separate application under the scheme. From time to time, the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, has selected eligible beneficiaries for housing based on the Social, Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011. 
 - For families who were left out in the SECC 2011 survey but were eligible for PMAY-G housing, the Government of India conducted the Awaas Plus Survey through a mobile app from July 2017 to 30 June 2018. Based on the Awaas Plus survey data, a permanent waitlist was prepared, and since the year 2020-21, housing targets have been allocated by the Government of India on the basis of this list. Currently, the financial assistance is being transferred directly to the bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.

documents_required: Documents are required as per the guidelines prescribed by the Government for this scheme.

faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries receive ₹130,000/- for constructing a house.
